meta_description: The Little Mermaid summary and lesson, the original Andersen story, and read-aloud tips to teach your child love and courage. A classic tale guide for ages 4-7.

content.alt: The Little Mermaid - What kind of story is The Little Mermaid?
content.text:
What kind of story is The Little Mermaid?

The Little Mermaid is an Andersen tale about a mermaid princess of the sea who falls in love with a human prince, gains legs, and comes up onto land. It is a masterpiece that beautifully portrays heartfelt love, courage, and the meaning of choice.
content.caption: Longing for the land

content.alt: The Little Mermaid - The original story of The Little Mermaid
content.text:
The original story of The Little Mermaid

The original is "Den lille Havfrue," published by Hans Christian Andersen in 1837. The original is famous for its bittersweet ending in which the mermaid turns to sea foam, but picture books for young children usually adapt it into something warmer. The bargain with the sea witch and the loss of her voice are central to the tale.
content.caption: A courageous choice

content.alt: The Little Mermaid - The Little Mermaid story summary
content.text:
The Little Mermaid story summary

The little mermaid rescues a human prince during a storm and comes to love him deeply. To become human, she makes a bargain with the sea witch, giving up her voice in exchange for legs so she can come onto land. The mermaid's love, as she strives to convey her true heart even without words, brings a quiet and moving tenderness.
content.caption: Love conveyed without words

content.alt: The Little Mermaid - The lesson of The Little Mermaid
content.text:
The lesson of The Little Mermaid

The core message is that heartfelt love and courage—and every choice—come with feeling and responsibility. Talk with your child by asking "Have you ever given something up for the sake of something precious?" and share the depths of the heart together.
content.caption: The courage love gave

content.alt: The Little Mermaid - How to read it aloud to your child
content.text:
How to read it aloud to your child

Read the underwater scenes in a mysterious, calm way, and the storm scenes with tension. In the scene where she loses her voice, open a conversation about empathy: "If you couldn't speak, how would you share what's in your heart?" Best suited for ages 4 to 7.
content.caption: Reading that shares the heart

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. What age is The Little Mermaid good for?
A. Best suited for ages 4 to 7. With its themes of love, courage, and choice, it is wonderful for a time when emotions are growing rich.

Q. I heard the original ending is sad?
A. The original has a bittersweet ending where she turns to sea foam, but picture books for young children usually adapt it into something warmer.

Q. What conversations pair well with it?
A. Talk together about "courage for the sake of something precious" and "how to share your heart without words."

Classic tales to read together

If you enjoyed this story, try reading these classic tales together too.

  • The Frog Prince
  • The Ant and the Grasshopper
  • The Selfish Giant
  • Gulliver's Travels
